title: Variables
goal: This lesson covers variables, which let you store a value once and reuse it wherever you need it.
learn: A variable is a named box that holds a value
Use = to store a value in it
Print the variable name to show what is inside
idea: A variable is a named box that holds a value. You put something in the box with =, and after that you can use the name instead of typing the value again. Text still needs quotes when you store it, but numbers do not. So name = "Ava" works and age = 11 works, but name = Ava would not.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change name = "Ava" to your own name and keep the quotes. Press Run and both lines that use name should update, which is the whole point of a variable.

practice.text: Store a name and an age in variables, then use ONE print to show them in a sentence. Fill in the blank.
practice.hint: Do not retype "Sam" or 11 inside print. Use the variable names name and age so Python shows whatever is stored.
practice.starterTip: Try: print(name, "is", age, "years old"). Commas add spaces between the words and numbers.
practice.starter:
name = "Sam"
age = 11
# One print that uses both variables
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if name and age are assigned to variables and a single print uses both variable names (not only hardcoded text for both).

practice.text: The colour variable is already set. Print a sentence that uses it.
practice.hint: Your print should include the variable colour, not only the word blue in quotes.
practice.starterTip: Example: print("My favourite colour is", colour). You can change the sentence, but keep colour in the print.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if a colour (or color) variable holds a non-empty string and print uses that variable name.

quiz.question: Which line correctly stores the text Maya in a variable called name?
quiz.correct: Right, the text needs quotes and the variable name goes on the left of the =.
quiz.wrong: The variable name goes on the left, and text values need quotes.

quiz.question: What is a variable?

options.text: A named box that holds a value
A blank line in the output

quiz.correct: Yes, a variable stores a value under a name you choose.
quiz.wrong: Think of a labeled box. The name is how you find the value again.

quiz.question: Why use a variable instead of typing the same value many times?

options.text: Python requires every value to be in a variable
So you can reuse the value by its name

quiz.correct: Right, a variable lets you reuse a value without rewriting it everywhere.
quiz.wrong: The main reason is reuse. It has nothing to do with speed or a Python rule.
